concepts.title: How Expressions are Formed
concepts.definition: Algebraic expressions are formed by combining variables and constants using operations (add, subtract, multiply, divide). x*x = x^2, x*x*x = x^3.
concepts.key_idea: Combine variables and constants with operations.
question_patterns: form expression from variables and constants
one half of sum of x and y
one fourth of product of p and q
x and y squared and added
5 added to three times product of m and n

solution_steps.explain: Find what changes (variable) and what is fixed (constant)
Determine which operations (add, subtract, multiply, divide) to use
Combine using the operations in correct order

concepts.title: Terms of an Expression
concepts.definition: Terms are parts of an expression formed separately and then added. Each term is a product of factors. The numerical factor is the coefficient.
concepts.formula: expression = sum of terms; term = product of factors
concepts.key_idea: Expression = sum of terms. Term = product of factors. Coefficient = numerical factor.
question_patterns: show terms and factors by tree diagram

solution_steps.explain: Separate parts connected by + or - (minus sign belongs to following term)
Each term is a product of factors (numerical and algebraic)

concepts.title: Like and Unlike Terms
concepts.definition: Like terms have the same algebraic factors (same variables with same powers). Unlike terms have different algebraic factors. Numerical coefficients and order of variables don't matter.
concepts.formula: like terms: same variables, same powers; unlike: different
concepts.key_idea: Like terms: same variables and powers. Coefficients don't matter.
question_patterns: are these like or unlike terms

solution_steps.explain: Powers of each variable must match
Same variables and powers = like terms. Otherwise unlike.

concepts.title: Monomials, Binomials, Trinomials, Polynomials
concepts.definition: Monomial: one term. Binomial: two unlike terms. Trinomial: three unlike terms. Polynomial: one or more terms (includes all of above).
concepts.formula: monomial=1 term; binomial=2 unlike; trinomial=3 unlike; polynomial=1+

solution_steps.explain: Count the number of unlike terms in the expression
1 = monomial, 2 = binomial, 3 = trinomial, 4+ = polynomial (not specifically named)
All classifications (monomial, binomial, trinomial) are types of polynomials, so confirm the expression is a polynomial with one or more unlike terms

concepts.title: Finding Value of an Expression
concepts.definition: To find the value of an expression, substitute the given value(s) of variable(s) and compute. For two variables, both values are needed.
concepts.formula: value = substitute variable values and compute
concepts.key_idea: Substitute variable values, then compute following order of operations.
question_patterns: find value of expression for x =
simplify and find value if x = 2
simplify and find value if x = 3 a = -1 b = -2
what should value of a if expression equals 5

solution_steps.explain: Replace each variable with its given value

worked_examples.question_pattern: identify terms which are not constants and give numerical coefficients

solution_template.explain: Identify terms that are pure numbers
Numerical factor of each non-constant term

worked_examples.question_pattern: what is the coefficient of {var} in {expression}

solution_template.explain: Identify which term contains the variable
The rest of the term (besides the variable) is the coefficient

worked_examples.question_pattern: state whether pairs are like or unlike terms with reasons

solution_template.explain: Check if variables and powers match

worked_examples.question_pattern: find value of expressions for x = {val}

solution_template.explain: Replace x with the given value

worked_examples.question_pattern: find value of expressions when n = {val}

solution_template.explain: Replace n with the given value

worked_examples.question_pattern: find value of expressions for a = {av}, b = {bv}

solution_template.explain: Replace a and b with given values
